question: Can the exact imported comparator assumptions support a useful conditional contract without assuming the promised preservation result?

assumptions.name: propext
assumptions.interpretation: For propositions a and b, logical equivalence implies equality. This is a target-theory assumption, not a claim about executable comparison or object-language axioms in an input artifact.
assumptions.discharge: Retain as an explicit foundation of the named host theory. Avoiding it would require a separately checked constructive/relation-based development; source review cannot discharge a foundation axiom.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co: axiom propext {a b : Prop} : (a ↔ b) → a = b
assumptions.declaration_text: axiom propext {a b : Prop} : (a ↔ b) → a = b

assumptions.name: Classical.choice
assumptions.interpretation: From Nonempty α for any Sort u, select an α. It supplies classical reasoning in host proofs; it does not assert an algorithm for selecting data or approve new object-language axioms.
assumptions.discharge: Retain as an explicit foundation. Constructive separation/completeness may be an alternative, but a full proof-term dependency graph and choice-free replacement were not extracted in this bounded review.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co: axiom Classical.choice {α : Sort u} : Nonempty α → α
assumptions.declaration_text: axiom Classical.choice {α : Sort u} : Nonempty α → α

assumptions.name: Quot.sound
assumptions.interpretation: Related elements are equal in the primitive quotient. It is a host-theory quotient principle. Function extensionality in Core uses it; no consistency proof follows.
assumptions.discharge: Retain the quotient foundation. Replacing function equalities with pointwise relations is a research alternative, not evidence that the pinned comparator reports no longer depend on this axiom.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co:
namespace Quot
axiom sound : ∀ {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {a b : α}, r a b → Quot.mk r a = Quot.mk r b
assumptions.declaration_text: axiom sound : ∀ {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {a b : α}, r a b → Quot.mk r a = Quot.mk r b

assumptions.name: Lean.Level.instLawfulBEqLevel
assumptions.interpretation: Assumes LawfulBEq for the particular BEq Level instance: Boolean self-equality is true and Boolean equality implies actual Lean.Level equality. The implementation is an opaque extern lean_level_eq. This is stronger than saying levels have equal numerical denotations; it is an unproved host primitive correspondence assumption.
assumptions.discharge: No proof of the opaque extern is available in the inspected sources. A new transparent structural equality with a proved lawfulness instance could support a changed comparator; equivalence to the existing extern would still need a separate bridge. Testing equality cannot prove this universal axiom.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co:
namespace Lean.Level
@[instance] axiom instLawfulBEqLevel : LawfulBEq Level

assumptions.name: Lean.Level.isExplicitSubsumedAux_eq
assumptions.interpretation: Extensional equality of the private partial array-scanning helper and its total copy, for all arrays, offsets and indices. The total recursion advances i and can use the remaining array length as a termination measure. The original helper is logically opaque; comparing the visible clauses is evidence for a correspondence hypothesis, not a Lean proof of that equality.
assumptions.discharge: Use a total helper directly in an explicit new comparator/model or formalize a source-to-runtime refinement. A local induction about the total copy does not prove equality to the imported opaque partial constant. No such discharge was checked here.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co:
namespace Lean.Level
@[simp] axiom isExplicitSubsumedAux_eq : isExplicitSubsumedAux = Total.isExplicitSubsumedAux

assumptions.name: Lean.Level.normalize_eq
assumptions.interpretation: Extensional equality between the core partial normalizer and Total.normalize. This is a substantial algorithm-to-logic bridge over every Level, not merely a termination annotation. The total body still calls private skipExplicit, isExplicitSubsumed and mkMaxAux; the axiom name does not imply that every helper bridge is proved or used by each target.
assumptions.discharge: A transparent total comparator could avoid the opaque normalizer, but would change the accepted strategy and require fresh proof and exact acceptance checks. Source similarity and finite tests are insufficient to discharge normalize_eq. Do not describe this assumption as already proved or trivial.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co:
namespace Lean.Level
axiom normalize_eq : normalize = Total.normalize

assumptions.name: Std.TreeMap.all_eq_all_toList
assumptions.interpretation: For arbitrary key/value types, comparison function, map and Boolean predicate, TreeMap.all equals List.all over the map entry list. This is a data-structure traversal bridge. Its source links a historical upstream issue; no current disposition was queried.
assumptions.discharge: Prove the map traversal lemma against pinned implementation internals or explicitly use toList.all in a successor comparator. Those internals are outside this source allocation; existing calls and the printed reports justify retaining it as conditional, not asserting discharge.
assumptions.exact_source_statement_with_namespace_co:
namespace Std.TreeMap
variable {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {cmp : α → α → Ordering} {t : TreeMap α β cmp}
axiom all_eq_all_toList {p : α → β → Bool} :
    t.all p = t.toList.all fun a => p a.1 a.2
assumptions.declaration_text:
axiom all_eq_all_toList {p : α → β → Bool} :
    t.all p = t.toList.all fun a => p a.1 a.2

dependency_evidence_scope: The retained CVC-3 stdout mechanically establishes all seven transitive leaves for both imported comparators. Source-visible paths explain uses but are not a reconstructed proof-term DAG. Verify.LevelStd internals remain uninspected; printed membership must not be relabeled as a complete intermediate path.
noncircularity: None of the seven exact statements mentions Lab.Accepts, Contract, EncodingTarget or PreservationTarget. The four helper axioms concern primitive equality, normalization/helper correspondence and map traversal. Conditional reuse still leaves owned-name encoding, positional evaluation and the fixed acceptance/boundary obligations to prove. Their lower-level scope does not establish their truth or joint consistency.

alternatives.reason: Keeps the exact semantic judgment and existing strategy while exposing the real assumption boundary. The minimal missing work is protocol/runner succession and the local proof, with finite ceilings and no new upstream compilation.

VerifyLevel exposes Normalize.normalize_eval/eval_congr and normalize_complete, suggesting a route that omits the core isEquiv fast path. No reduced axiom closure was printed, the acceptance definition would change, and all_eq_all_toList remains visibly used. Do not claim an assumption-free replacement.

Proving equality to opaque extern/partial constants needs more than Lab proof edits: a changed transparent implementation or an explicit refinement model and separate source scope. It is higher-cost and not necessary for a clearly conditional result.

A small non-circular encoding-to-comparator bridge remains useful for the existing imax artifact ambiguity. Stop remains mandatory if the new baseline differs, the finite proof bound is exhausted, or no useful scoped result remains.
